raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's farming. I'm 62, been working these 2.2 mu for 40 years — I know this land better than my own hands. Just me and my wife at home now, kids are off in the city doing factory work. So all the work falls on us two old folks, but 2.2 mu isn't much, we manage.

The wheat's already in the ground — I put it in last October like always, right after the maize came off. Used seed from the agri shop in town, same variety everyone in our village uses, nothing fancy. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that 15-15-15 kind, one bag covers a bit more than a mu. My neighbor Old Wang does the same, has done for years, and his wheat comes out fine.

Right now the wheat is greening up nicely after winter. In two or three weeks when it starts jointing, I'll topdress with urea — about half a bag per mu, maybe a little more if it looks pale. Urea prices went up again this year, so I can't be too generous. Have to watch every yuan.

For water, the wheat already got one irrigation before winter, and I'll water it again at green-up and once more when the grain is filling. Three times should do. The well water costs money now — pumping fee keeps going up and the water table drops every year. Can't waste it. Some younger farmers irrigate four or five times but I don't see the point for a yield that's not gonna be that much higher.

Weeds I spray once in early spring with herbicide from town, costs maybe 20 yuan per mu. Don't bother with fungicide unless I see disease — usually don't. Last year I got about 420 kg per mu, year before 440. This year if the weather's normal I expect the same.

First week of June the wheat comes off. I hire the combine — everyone does, way too much work to cut by hand at my age. Right after, within a few days, I have the machine come direct-seed maize into the wheat stubble. No time to plow, no need either. That's how we all do it now for twenty years.

Maize seed is hybrid — you have to buy fresh every year, can't save it. About 40 yuan per mu for good seed. Same fertilizer pattern as wheat — one bag compound at planting, urea topdress when the maize is knee-high. Maize doesn't drink as much as wheat and we usually get summer rain, so maybe one irrigation in July if it's dry, that's it. I watch for corn borer around tasseling time and spray insecticide if I see it.

Maize usually gives me 480-500 kg per mu, better than the wheat. Between the two crops I can bring in around 4,000-5,000 yuan if prices hold. Input costs eat up maybe 1,700 of that. Not much left for two old people, but we don't need much, and the kids send some money home for New Year.
